mcq.QUESTION_DESC: Which expansion would you use for \( f(x) = x^2 \) on \( (0, L) \) if you want a series with only cosine terms?
For \( f(x) = \sin(x) \) on \( (0, \pi) \), which expansion would be most appropriate?
When finding half-range expansions, we extend \( f(x) \) to \( (-L, L) \) to make it:
If \( f(x) \) is given on \( (0, L) \) and you want a series that converges to \( f(x) \) at \( x=0 \), which expansion should you use?
For \( f(x) \) defined on \( (0, L) \) with \( f(0)=0 \), which expansion is guaranteed to converge to \( f(x) \) at \( x=0 \)?

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(a_0 = \frac{2}{L} \int_0^{L/2} k dx = k\)

(2 Mark)

\(a_n = \frac{2}{L} \int_0^{L/2} k \cos(\frac{n\pi x}{L}) dx = \frac{2k}{n\pi} \sin(\frac{n\pi}{2})\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{For even } n: a_n=0; \text{ for odd } n=2m-1: a_n = \frac{2k}{(2m-1)\pi}(-1)^{m+1}\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Thus } f(x) = \frac{k}{2} + \frac{2k}{\pi}\sum_{m=1}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^{m+1}}{2m-1} \cos(\frac{(2m-1)\pi x}{L})\)

(2 Mark)

sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{When would you choose half-range series over full Fourier series?}\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(b_n = \frac{2}{L} \int_0^{L} 1 \cdot \sin(\frac{n\pi x}{L}) dx\)

(2 Mark)

\(= \frac{2}{L} \left[ -\frac{L}{n\pi} \cos(\frac{n\pi x}{L}) \right]_0^L\)

(2 Mark)

\(= \frac{2}{n\pi} [1 - \cos(n\pi)] = \frac{2}{n\pi}[1 - (-1)^n]\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Thus } 1 = \frac{4}{\pi}\sum_{n=\text{odd}} \frac{1}{n} \sin(\frac{n\pi x}{L})\)

(2 Mark)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{Given half-range sine series } f(x) = \sum b_n \sin(\frac{n\pi x}{L}), \text{ find } b_n \text{ if } f(x) = 1.\)

lq.QUESTION_DESC: Find the Fourier series for \(f(x)=\begin{cases} \pi+x, & -\pi\leq x\leq0 \\ \pi-x, & 0\leq x\leq\pi \end{cases}\) and deduce that \(\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{(2n-1)^2}=\frac{\pi^2}{8}\).

lq.ANSWER:
StepMarks
Sine series: \(b_n=\frac{2}{\pi}\int_0^{\pi}f(x)\sin nx\,dx\)(1)
Compute: \(b_n=\frac{4}{\pi n^2}\sin\frac{n\pi}{2}\)(4)
Cosine series: \(a_0=\frac{2}{\pi}\int_0^{\pi}f(x)dx=\frac{\pi}{2}\)(2)
\(a_n=\frac{2}{\pi}\int_0^{\pi}f(x)\cos nx\,dx=\frac{2}{\pi n^2}\left[2\cos\frac{n\pi}{2}-1-(-1)^n\right]\)(4)
Write both series explicitly(4)
